description:
About the Position

This Liverpool–AFBI studentship investigates metabolic responses to methane-suppressing feed additives in beef cattle. It is advertised for UK students who meet the stated eligibility requirements. University of Liverpool invites applications for a PhD position in this area: Cattle Metabolomics and Methane Mitigation at University of Liverpool, UK. Research areas covered include Bioinformatics, Biology. The host institution is in Liverpool, United Kingdom. The opportunity is fully funded; financial support is listed as Covered. Interested candidates should note the deadline: 31 October 2026.

Official Project Title

Livestock Metabolomics: Investigating Metabolic Signatures of Methane Mitigation in Beef Cattle

Research Focus and Methods

Profile biological samples across the production cycle and integrate metabolomics with methane emissions, microbiome information and animal performance. Investigate biomarkers associated with mitigation, health and feed efficiency.

Research Training and Development

Research includes field and laboratory work at AFBI in Northern Ireland and metabolomics analysis at Liverpool.

Funding and Duration

Studentship funding and award conditions
ComponentDetails
AwardPhD studentship; selection is competitive
ProgrammeAFBI-funded studentship
DurationFour years
StipendA living stipend is funded for four years; the advert does not publish a numeric annual rate.
Tuition and research supportAFBI funds tuition fees and a four-year stipend, provided eligibility is met.
Award conditionsSelection is competitive; an advertised project does not guarantee a studentship.

Eligibility and English Language

Applicant qualifications and funding eligibility
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityUK students meeting the advert’s eligibility rules; applicants from Northern Ireland and the island of Ireland are encouraged to apply subject to those rules.
Academic preparationAt least a 2:1-equivalent honours degree in Animal Science, Chemistry, Biology, Biochemistry or a related biological discipline.
Project interests and skillsInterest in animal research, mass spectrometry and quantitative biological analysis.
English languageMeet the host university’s English-language admission rules. An approved alternative or exemption may apply; IELTS is not universally mandatory.

About University of Liverpool

The University of Liverpool is a public research university in Liverpool, England, and a member of the Russell Group. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral study across health, science, engineering, business, humanities and social sciences. Its research and teaching connect specialist expertise with challenges facing communities, industry and society internationally.

Official website: https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/

Application Dates and Location

Deadline, start date and research location

Application deadline31 October 2026

Research locationLiverpool, United Kingdom

Contact

  • Email: howbeer.muhamad-ali@liverpool.ac.uk
  • Email: seyedali.goldansaz@afbini.gov.uk
  • Email: omarcristobal.carballo@afbini.gov.uk

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be sent to the contacts above or raised through the channel given on the official announcement page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 31 October 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
  • Review the eligibility criteria carefully; applications outside the stated scope are usually rejected at the first screening stage.

How to Apply

  1. Email Dr Howbeer Muhamadali and Dr Seyed Ali Goldansaz using the official advert’s addresses.
  2. Include your CV, cover letter, a relevant research proposal of no more than two pages and two reference letters.
  3. Follow the university’s subsequent online application instructions.

Application Checklist

  • CV
  • Cover letter
  • Relevant research proposal, maximum two pages
  • Two reference letters covering academic potential and professional suitability
